chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

That which the creatures are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of Allah (Exalted is His Glory), that is what they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him); and just as they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Messenger (peace be upon him), so too they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Imam; and just as they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the Imam, so too they are not able to grasp the essence of the attribute of the believer.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the attributes of Allah, the Prophet, the Imam, and the believer in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Sifat* by extending the incomprehensibility of Divine attributes through a hierarchical chain: from Allah to the Prophet, then to the Imam, and finally to the believer. It underscores the concept of *Haqiqah Muhammadiyya* and *Haqiqah Alawiyya*, where the spiritual reality of the Imam and the faithful reflects the Divine essence without being identical to it, preserving both continuity and distinction. This establishes the believer as the ultimate locus of divine manifestation, linking cosmic theology with individual spiritual potential.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 59. It has been narrated that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:

Just as people are not able to describe the real essence of Allah [M.G], similarly they cannot describe the true nature of the Messenger of Allah (a.s); and just as they are unable to describe the true nature of the Messenger of Allah (a.s), similarly they cannot possibly grasp the essential being of an Imam; and just as they cannot possibly grasp the essential being of an Imam, similarly they can never understand the true nature of a believer
